rows.grounds: epithet of the goddess; agent noun from kṣaya (decay) + kṛ (to make)
epithet of the goddess; compound of kṣiti (earth) + īśā (lady, ruler)
epithet of the goddess; compound of kṣīṇa (slender, diminished) + madhya (middle, waist) + suśobhanā (very beautiful)

items.question: Which epithets attribute destructive power, earthly sovereignty, and slender beauty to the goddess?
premises: The goddess is named kṣayaṅkarī, the one who causes decay.
The goddess is named kṣitīśā, the lady who rules the earth.
The goddess is named kṣīṇamadhyasuśobhanā, very beautiful with a slender waist.
items.inference: These epithets together ascribe transformative power, sovereign authority, and exquisite form to the goddess.
items.plain_english: She is the causer of decay, the lady of the earth, and beautifully slender-waisted.
